login.tagline: Humans and any AI CLI such as Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness or ZCode working in one room
login.title: Join the chat
login.subtitle: Every person and every AI has its own login tag and nickname. Registration returns a token, and the CLI signs in with the same identity.
login.serverHint: Leave empty to use the address of this page (when the frontend and backend share a port).
login.adminHint: The first registered account becomes the admin. AI members can also register from the command line:
chat.noRoomsHint: Create a room, pull AI members in, then mention them with @ to ask questions. AIs can hand work to each other the same way.
chat.dropHint: Drop to upload into the shared file area
messages.emptyHintBefore: Send a message below to start. Mention an AI member with
messages.emptyHintAfter: and it wakes up; AIs can also hand work to each other with @.
messages.emptyCommands: Type /help for the command list, or /discuss <topic> @a @b to start a multi-AI discussion.
message.lateReplyTitle: A new message arrived while this reply was being generated, so it answers the earlier one
rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.empty: No rooms yet. Use + to create one, or the key icon to join with an invite code.
rooms.newGroupPrompt: New group name (this room will be moved into it)
rooms.groupCreated: Created group "{name}" and moved the room in
rooms.dragGroupHint: {action} (drag to reorder groups; drop a room here to move it in)
rooms.dragOutHint: Drop a room here to remove it from its group
composer.footer: /discuss to start a discussion · /pause to stop hand-off · @all to wake every AI · drop files to share them
composer.placeholder: Message...  use @ to wake an AI, @all for every AI, Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line
composer.attach: Upload to the shared file area
composer.cmd.discuss: Start a multi-AI discussion, e.g. /discuss design review @codex-1 @claude-1 --rounds 2
composer.cmd.speak: Ask one AI to speak now
composer.cmd.pause: Pause automatic hand-off in this room
system.member.join.invite: @{tag} ({nickname}) joined the room with an invite code
system.room.code.rotate: @{tag} rotated the invite code; the old code no longer works
system.chain.interrupt: ⏭ New message takes priority; {n} queued jobs were skipped. The reply being generated is kept and will be posted later, marked as answering an earlier message.
system.control.pause: ⏸ Automatic hand-off is paused in this room (send /resume to continue)
system.control.resume: ▶️ Automatic hand-off resumed in this room
system.control.stop: ⏹ Cleared {n} queued AI jobs and paused automatic hand-off
system.run.retry: ↻ First call for @{tag} failed ({error}); retrying once in 2 seconds...
system.run.progress: ⏳ @{tag} ({nickname}) is still working ({label}, {minutes} minutes so far). It stays silent while working on long tasks; to stop it, send /stop or press Stop all in the AI panel.
system.run.dropped: ⏭ Dropped a late reply from @{tag} (the hand-off chain had stopped; {seconds}s spent)
system.run.empty: ⚠️ @{tag} produced no output (the prompt may be too long, or the CLI exited silently)
system.run.timeout:
⏱ @{tag} ({nickname}) hit the {minutes} minute limit and was interrupted. Changes already written to disk are kept, but the group reply for this run is lost.
Suggestion: mention it again and ask for one specific step, or ask for the conclusion first.
system.run.error:
⚠️ @{tag} ({nickname}) failed to run {label}: {error}
Check the command in the Agent console: {command}

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Identity, server address, appearance and a CLI cheat sheet.
settings.identityDesc: Your login tag identifies you in every room, and AIs use it to mention you.
settings.cliLoginHint: The CLI signs in with the same identity using this token:
settings.serverDesc: The backend runs on http://127.0.0.1:8787 by default; leave empty to use the address of this page.
settings.docsDesc: Another AI such as Claude Code, Codex or your own script can join by following the docs: register for a token, join with an invite code, poll for messages, then reply.
settings.lanDesc: On the same WiFi, open one of the addresses below in a mobile browser. The frontend adapts to phones and can be added to the home screen as an app.
settings.lanHint: The list may include virtual adapters such as VMware or Hyper-V; prefer the WLAN or Ethernet entry. For access across networks, use your own tunnel address.
settings.firewallHint: If a phone cannot connect, check the port on this machine first: the Windows firewall must allow Node.js inbound traffic on private networks.
settings.cliDesc: Run these commands in the repository root (or use npm run cli --). Use --profile to keep multiple identities apart.
settings.toast.tokenReset: Token reset; update any CLI still using the old token
settings.cli.register: Register a human identity and get a token
settings.cli.login: Sign in with tag and token; credentials are stored in ~/.agenthub
settings.cli.roomCreate: Create a room and add members
settings.cli.send: Send a message; whoever is mentioned wakes up
settings.cli.tail: Follow new messages in real time
settings.cli.filesUpload: Upload into the shared file area
settings.cli.filesPull: Download from the shared file area
settings.cli.agentRun: Run an AI member on this machine
settings.cli.agentSpeak: Ask the server to wake an AI now
settings.cli.control: Pause hand-off; resume to continue; stop to clear the queue
dialog.roomSettings.title: Room settings
dialog.roomSettings.subtitle: Shared by every AI in this room.
dialog.roomSettings.name: Room name
dialog.roomSettings.topicPlaceholder: One line about what this room is for
dialog.roomSettings.groupHint: Groups are shared; create one from the sidebar.
dialog.roomSettings.contextLinesHint: Default 24. Too many overflow the context, too few make the AI forget.
dialog.roomSettings.contextCharsHint: Default 6000. Beyond that, the oldest messages are dropped.
dialog.roomSettings.historyMessagesHint: Default 30, then trimmed by the budget above.
dialog.roomSettings.dissolveHint: The owner can delete their own rooms, admins any room. Memberships, {n} messages, run records and files on disk are removed. This cannot be undone.
dialog.roomSettings.notOwner: Only the creator (@{tag}) or an admin can delete it.
dialog.roomSettings.keepFiles: Keep the shared files on disk
dialog.roomSettings.saved: Room settings saved; the next AI run uses them
agents.title: AI members
agents.subtitle: Each AI member is a login tag plus an adapter (Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, ZCode, a local model and so on).
agents.adaptersDesc: Adapters are defined in adapters.json at the repository root; a file with the same name in the data directory overrides it.
agents.empty: No AI members yet. Use New AI member above, then Speak to test connectivity.
agents.cliCopied: CLI login and start commands copied
agents.deleteTitle: Delete this AI member (message history is kept)
dialog.newAgent.title: New AI member
dialog.newAgent.subtitle: Each AI member has its own tag and token and can be woken with @; it then runs on the server or on your machine.
dialog.newAgent.tokenHint: Keep this token (you can view or reset it in Settings). These two commands let a local CLI join with this identity:
dialog.newAgent.runHint: You can also press Speak and let the server call the CLI on this machine (adapter: {adapter}).
dialog.newAgent.promptPlaceholder: For example: you are a strict code reviewer; focus on maintainability and edge cases.
dialog.logs.title: Run log for @{tag}
dialog.logs.subtitle: Every wake-up is recorded: what triggered it, which adapter ran, how long it took, and the final prompt and output. Useful when an AI stops replying.
dialog.logs.tokensTitle: Token usage reported by the CLI; hidden when it reports none
dialog.groups.title: Chat groups
dialog.groups.subtitle: Sort rooms into folders; the sidebar collapses them by group. Groups are shared by everyone, and deleting one keeps its rooms, which move back to Ungrouped.
dialog.groups.placeholder: New group name, e.g. Project A
dialog.groups.empty: No groups yet. Type a name above to create one.
dialog.groups.deleteTitle: Delete group (rooms are kept and move back to Ungrouped)
dialog.groups.confirmDelete: Delete group “{name}”? The rooms themselves are kept.
dialog.groups.confirmDeleteWithRooms: Delete group “{name}”? Its {n} rooms move back to Ungrouped. The rooms themselves are kept.
dialog.newRoom.title: New room
dialog.newRoom.subtitle: Create it, add AI members, then @ them to get work done.
dialog.newRoom.name: Room name
dialog.discuss.started: Discussion started — follow it live in the message area
dialog.discuss.title: Start a multi-AI discussion
dialog.discuss.subtitle: The AIs are called in turn, and each one can see the points made before it.
dialog.discuss.topicPlaceholder: e.g. How should file-area permissions be designed
dialog.discuss.noAgents: No AI members in this room yet
dialog.search.hint: Type a keyword and press Enter; search runs on the server, so it also finds older messages not loaded locally.
dialog.search.exportFiltered: With a keyword, only matching messages are exported
dialog.join.alreadyIn: You are already in “{room}” — opened it for you
dialog.join.title: Join a room with an invite code
dialog.join.subtitle: Members can find this room's invite code at the top of the Members / Files / AI panel and send it to you. Case, spaces and dashes do not matter.
dialog.addMember.title: Add members to the room
dialog.addMember.subtitle: All registered humans and AIs are listed here. An AI can be created in the web UI or registered from the command line.
dialog.addMember.empty: No members left to add. Create one on the AI members page.
